title: break & continue
summary: Loop control: `break` exits the loop immediately; `continue` (Luau) skips the rest of the current iteration and jumps to the next one.

syntax:
for i = 1, 10 do
    if i > 5 then break end        -- stop entirely
    if i % 2 == 0 then continue end -- skip this iteration
    print(i)                        -- prints 1, 3, 5
end

details.heading: continue is Luau-only
details.body: Classic Lua 5.1 has no `continue` — you'll see older code emulate it with `repeat ... until true` + break. In Luau just use `continue`.

details.heading: Innermost loop only
details.body: Both statements affect only the loop they're directly inside. In nested loops, use flags or restructure if you need to break two levels.

explanation.whatItIs: `break` is the emergency exit; `continue` is 'skip ahead to the next round'. Together they let loops stop early or filter work.
explanation.whyItExists: Searching: stop when found. Filtering: ignore cases you don't care about without nesting everything in an if.
whenToUse: `break` after finding what you searched for
`continue` to invert guard conditions: `if dead then continue end`
Bailing out of expensive loops when the goal is already met
whenNotToUse: Don't sprinkle breaks everywhere 'to be safe' — it makes loop flow unreadable
Don't use break/continue to compensate for a wrong loop condition; fix the condition
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
    if player.Team ~= myTeam then continue end  -- skip others
    if player.Name == target then
        found = player
        break                                   -- stop searching
    end
end
```
continue = 'next, please'. break = 'we're done here'.
tips: `continue` must be the last statement of its block (like return) — wrap logic accordingly
A loop that always breaks on iteration one is really an `if` in disguise
commonMistakes: Placing `continue` mid-block with code after it — parse error; restructure with if/else
Expecting break to exit nested loops — it exits only the innermost

examples.title: Find the first matching part
examples.code:
local found = nil
for _, child in workspace:GetChildren() do
    if not child:IsA("BasePart") then continue end
    if child.Name == "GoldenCoin" then
        found = child
        break   -- no need to keep scanning
    end
end
print(found and `Found at {found.Position}` or "Not found")
